topic: ARDS: Definition, Pathophysiology, and Risk Stratification
domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: State the Berlin definition PaO2/FiO2 thresholds for mild, moderate, and severe ARDS.
rationale: Berlin 2012 definition stratified ARDS by P/F ratio; severity predicts mortality and guides escalation to prone positioning and neuromuscular blockade.
confusable_with: Cardiogenic pulmonary edema (elevated PCWP, responds to diuresis)

topic: ARDS: Definition, Pathophysiology, and Risk Stratification
domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: What two mechanisms cause pulmonary edema, and which characterizes ARDS?
answer: (1) Increased hydrostatic pressure (cardiogenic); (2) Increased alveolar-capillary membrane permeability (non-cardiogenic/ARDS). ARDS is the permeability type.
rationale: In ARDS, inflammatory injury increases permeability regardless of PCWP; protein-rich fluid floods alveoli causing non-cardiogenic edema.
confusable_with: Cardiogenic pulmonary edema (hydrostatic, responds to diuresis/preload reduction)

topic: ARDS: Definition, Pathophysiology, and Risk Stratification
domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: What tidal volume strategy has the greatest evidence-based outcome benefit in ARDS?
answer: Lung-protective ventilation with tidal volumes of 6 mL/kg IBW; greatest improvement in mortality of any ARDS intervention in RCTs.
rationale: Low TV reduces volutrauma and barotrauma; ARDSnet trial showed ~22% relative mortality reduction vs. conventional 12 mL/kg TV.

topic: ARDS: Definition, Pathophysiology, and Risk Stratification
domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: What lung-protective ventilation parameters are targeted in ARDS management?
answer: TV 6 mL/kg IBW, plateau pressure <30 cmH2O, higher PEEP, permissive hypercapnia and lower PaO2 accepted.
rationale: Limiting plateau pressure prevents barotrauma; higher PEEP recruits collapsed alveoli; permissive hypercapnia avoids volutrauma from normalization attempts.

topic: ARDS: Definition, Pathophysiology, and Risk Stratification
domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: At what FiO2 level and duration does pulmonary oxygen toxicity become concerning?
answer: FiO2 >50-60% for prolonged periods (beyond 10-20 hours at 100% O2 is generally safe); toxicity mediated by reactive oxygen species.
rationale: High FiO2 generates superoxide, hydroxyl radicals, and hydrogen peroxide that damage alveolar epithelium; ARDS management targets minimizing FiO2 with PEEP.

topic: Abdominal Compartment Syndrome and Intraabdominal Hypertension
domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: Define intraabdominal hypertension (IAH) and abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS) by pressure thresholds.
answer: IAH: sustained IAP >12 mmHg. ACS: sustained IAP >20 mmHg associated with new organ dysfunction/failure. Normal IAP is ~5 mmHg.
rationale: Progressive IAH impairs venous drainage and organ perfusion; ACS threshold marks the point where new organ failure begins.

topic: Abdominal Compartment Syndrome and Intraabdominal Hypertension
domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: What is the mechanism by which elevated IAP causes renal impairment?
answer: Elevated IAP impairs venous drainage from the kidney by compressing the renal vein, causing renal ischemia and oliguria.
rationale: Renal venous hypertension from IAP reduces filtration pressure; renal autoregulation fails once IAP chronically elevates.

topic: Abdominal Compartment Syndrome and Intraabdominal Hypertension
domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: Name four risk factors for IAH/ACS in the ICU.
answer: Massive fluid resuscitation, mechanical ventilation with high PEEP, abdominal surgery with tight closure, major trauma/burns, high BMI, prone positioning.
rationale: These factors either increase abdominal content (fluid/gas) or reduce abdominal wall compliance, raising intraabdominal pressure.

topic: Abdominal Compartment Syndrome and Intraabdominal Hypertension
domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: How does laparoscopic insufflation pressure above 25 cmH2O affect hemodynamics?
answer: Collapses major abdominal veins (IVC), reducing venous return, preload, and cardiac output; may also produce intraabdominal compartment syndrome.
rationale: High insufflation pressure exceeds venous pressure, compressing the IVC; reduced preload drops CO similar to ACS.

topic: Abdominal Compartment Syndrome and Intraabdominal Hypertension
domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: In bowel volvulus repair, what postoperative complication may prevent abdominal closure?
answer: Bowel edema post-reduction can prevent primary fascial closure and cause abdominal compartment syndrome if closure is forced.
rationale: Edematous bowel increases intraabdominal volume; forced tight closure risks ACS; temporary closure strategies (vacuum-assisted) allow edema resolution.
